thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 — KV cache prefetch entropy threshold breach. Continuous-batch sizes ramping across multiple shards, causing latency cliffs and downstream OOMs. Affected models: mistral-1.0, qwen-2.1, llama-3b. Auto-alerts triggered in us-west-2.
Samantha: seeing steady rise in kv_cache.size and prefetched prefixes. prefetched_count up 8x in 3m. small requests ballooning into giant batches.
Jamal: confirmed. tail latency for mistral-1.0 jumped from 40ms -> 1.2s. GQA requests are noisier but MQA correlated with prefetch growth.
Lia: oncall here, starting triage. Are we sure this is prefetch and not a recent rollout? any canary rollouts in the last hour?
Samantha: no model rollouts in last 2h. We shipped a metric-only change to the prefetch controller yesterday but not rollout. But someone flipped a runtime flag in us-west-2 at 09:10 (unknown owner).
Tien: digging into audit logs now. I see an API call: `PATCH /admin/flags` setting `prefetch_entropy_factor` to `0.9` at 09:11 from svc-ci. That would make prefetch more aggressive.
Michael: that explains it. Higher entropy factor expands candidate prefixes -> more KV load -> continuous-batch merging across requests.
Jamal: customer impact: a few mid-tier customers reporting increased error rates and >500ms latency on embeddings endpoints. Support ticket count +3 in last 10m. We should notify customer-facing team.
support-notify-bot: Notifying Support rotation and creating incident_#2659876543 in PagerDuty.
Lia: mitigation plan: 1) throttle prefetch on control plane globally to normal baseline 2) reduce continuous-batching window for affected models 3) scale Dedicated shard pool briefly to absorb current pressure 4) confirm KV eviction policy hasn't regressed.
Samantha: quick rollback: set prefetch_entropy_factor back to 0.55 (previous baseline). Running command now.
Samantha: ```
# admin API rollback
curl -X PATCH "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/flags" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prefetch_entropy_factor": 0.55}'
``` 
Samantha: patched flag; control plane acknowledged. Watching metrics.
Tien: reducing continuous-batch window for mistral-1.0 and qwen-2.1 to 50ms -> should reduce batch coalescing.
Tien: ```
runtimectl set-batch-config --model mistral-1.0 --window-ms 50 --max-batch-tokens 512
runtimectl set-batch-config --model qwen-2.1 --window-ms 50 --max-batch-tokens 1024
``` 
Jamal: scaling Dedicated shard pool +2 nodes in us-west-2 as buffer.
Michael: KV eviction rates spiked earlier but look back to normal now. Prefetch rollback appears to reduce new prefetched prefixes.
Samantha: metrics update: prefetched_count down 78% in 6m. continuous_batch_size p50 dropped from 22 -> 5. latency tail improving.
Lia: good. Can we put an emergency guard in the control plane to reject entropy_factor > 0.75 until we have safety checks?
Samantha: yes, I'll create a short-lived server-side limit and a validation error.
Samantha: ```
# reject high prefetch values
POST /admin/flags/guard
{ "flag": "prefetch_entropy_factor", "max": 0.75, "mode": "enforce" }
``` 
Tien: guard in place. Any downstream failures to surface to customers we need to escalate?
Jamal: Support: sending templated update to affected customers: brief incident summary, mitigation steps, ETA for follow-up (/incidents/email-draft in slack). Lia please approve.
Lia: lgtm minor edits. Include note that we rolled back control-plane flag and scaled pool, and that team will run postmortem.
support-notify-bot: Draft message queued: "We experienced degraded inference latency due to an internal prefetch tuning change; we've rolled back the change and applied temporary rate-limits. We'll follow up with root cause and steps to prevent recurrence." (ticket ids attached)
Michael: Post-mitigation checks: running load test against qwen-2.1 and mistral-1.0 to validate no regressions in throughput.
Michael: load test result quick check: p99 latency back within SLO for both models, CPU/GPU utilization normal. No error spikes.
Samantha: leaving canary on for 15m; if stable we'll close P1 and transition to follow-up action items.
Lia: next steps for postmortem: - timeline capture - why the svc-ci call allowed high entropy - add server-side validation - add a metric alert on prefetched_count/continuous_batch_size ratio - assign owner for prefetch controller
Jamal: assigning owners: Samantha lead remediation + guard, Tien audit + IAM rule for flags, Michael tests and follow-ups, Lia PM for customer comms and postmortem.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced. Will remain in P1-watching state until 2659876743.
Samantha: quick log snippet from control plane showing the offending call and rollback:
```
2026-03-15T09:11:23Z svc-ci PATCH /admin/flags {"prefetch_entropy_factor":0.9} -> 200
2026-03-15T09:17:02Z Samantha PATCH /admin/flags {"prefetch_entropy_factor":0.55} -> 200
```
Lia: capturing this for postmortem notes. Any lingering items?
Jamal: watch for any residual eviction churn and customer reopens. I'll stay on follow-up for 2h.
Samantha: ack. I'll open follow-up ticket with steps and include playbook for prefetched prefix limits. Adding link to evaluation harness to run pre-deploy safety tests.
support-notify-bot: Support notified customers; escalation channel opened.
oncall-bot: Handoff to next rotation at 2659876800. Filing final update and creating postmortem draft.
Samantha: thanks team. closing active mitigation thread, continuing follow-ups in #postmortems and #eng-runtime. :thumbsup:
